description:
## Objective and authorization
Make Zaq.Channels.JidoChatBridge a genuinely provider-neutral consumer of the jido_chat_* adapter family, including WhatsApp, Telegram and Mattermost. Standardize the contracts in jido_chat and implement WhatsApp-specific behavior inside jido_chat_whatsapp. Preserve the sole adapter-to-host callback option, sink_mfa. The user requested this implementation handoff after reviewing PR https://github.com/www-zaq-ai/zaq/pull/847 and discussing the design/examples. This turn authorizes Beadwork planning only: no implementation, test edits, commits, pushes, publishing, PR changes or merges have been performed or authorized by ticket creation.

## Verified baseline and related work
Research baseline: ZAQ 8714d6c763dc1da0ac11e0f3acfde05d89151663, matching PR #847; sibling ../jido_chat f154f07464377ecd8d81c6dd0de1b8af016fa616; ../jido_chat_whatsapp 7d6cb1d5901180c28961614c45d7e4dbdfe8301a. These match ZAQ mix.lock. ../jido_chat_mattermost and deps/jido_chat_telegram were comparison sources. Recheck these before implementation; do not assume a moving PR/branch still matches.
Related historical epic zaq-hce is closed but records a rejected/reverted multi-MFA approach. Read its description and relevant children; its old completion/validation claims do not prove this design implemented. Never reintroduce persist_mfa, activate_mfa, storage_mfa or compatibility shims for that rejected interface. Its historical no-test-edit scope is not blanket approval for test changes in this work; observe all currently applicable user constraints and the existing-test-behavior approval gate. Related zaq-0l7 / zaq-0l7.24 own earlier linked-device work and outstanding feature validation; do not duplicate their runtime or silently close their pending gates.

## Observed coupling / source map
ZAQ lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge.ex: from_listener/3,4 matches Jido.Chat.WhatsApp.Pairing.Request and Storage.Request; build_runtime_specs/2 calls storage_runtime_spec; prepare_listener_opts/3 and linked_device_listener_opts/3 construct history options; saved_connection_options/2 calls prepare_connection; connection_profile/1 depends on concrete adapter helpers; handle_message_event/4 branches on :whatsapp; logout probes an undeclared helper. handle_connection_action/3 and adapter_call_opts/2 assume linked-device/profile semantics.
lib/zaq/channels/bridge.ex fetch_connection_details_for_config/1 has a linked-device branch calling JidoChatBridge.connection_profile/1. Include this downstream coupling, not just the request structs.
lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/state.ex owns serialized chat state and lifecycle source/attempt fencing; provider wording in status should be generic when this path is touched.
Core ../jido_chat/lib/jido/chat/adapter.ex already defines optional authenticate/3 (wrapper authenticate/4), listener_child_specs/2 and sink_mfa invocation conventions. This is authentication, NOT an authorization callback: the host must authorize each command. Core's guides/authentication.md still describes persistence/activation callbacks and must be reconciled with the single-sink contract.
WhatsApp lib/jido_chat_whatsapp/adapter.ex, pairing_session.ex, pairing/request.ex, storage/request.ex, storage/split.ex, storage/runtime.ex, connection_worker.ex and message.ex own transport/storage implementation. Existing message normalization already supplies was_mentioned, author.is_me, channel_meta.is_dm and metadata.history.

## Required design (proposed API names, not shipped contracts)
1. Core-owned typed Authentication.Request and Storage.Request replace concrete WhatsApp request types at the host boundary. Preserve version/id fields, redacted Inspect, opaque host context/binding, bounded operations and existing sanitized results. Authentication operations persist/start remain distinct; storage operations bind/get/put/put_many/delete/delete_namespace/clear/list_keys retain absence/error semantics. A private typed envelope is not itself authority.
2. One sink_mfa, same invocation: apply(module, function, configured_args ++ [payload, opts]). No extra host callback MFA options and no provider-selected execution modules/functions from untrusted data. Host dispatch recognizes shared private request types before serialized State routing. Ordinary payloads and EventEnvelope/ActionEvent keep their existing route. Public listener/webhook ingress must reject private requests. Trusted sink scope fixes provider and, for saved connectors, connector identity; revalidate current actor/binding for every operation. Merely is_reference(runtime_reference) is not proof of authority.
3. Extend Jido.Chat.Adapter with minimal OPTIONAL documented contracts and wrappers for connection preparation, provider infrastructure specs, opaque connection identity, and explicit logout. Suggested shape: prepare_connection(opts) -> {:ok, opts} | {:error, reason}; provider_child_specs(opts) -> {:ok, specs} | {:error, reason}; connection_identity(binding) -> {:ok, opaque_identity} | {:error, reason}; logout(listener) -> :ok | {:error, reason}. Resolve exact signatures consistently before implementing; conversation snippets were schematic. Legacy defaults: unchanged opts, no infrastructure children, unsupported identity/logout. Preserve listener_child_specs/2 and authenticate/3. Callback declarations are behaviour functions, not new host MFA configuration.
4. jido_chat owns data contracts, validation and delegation only, not a new supervision tree, retry queue or pairing runtime. WhatsApp owns protocol, QR/session lifetime, profile derivation, Split/Mnesia, serialization, namespace routing, storage readiness and transport recovery. Host owns supervision/execution and deployment policy. Existing bounded WhatsApp request execution can call pure shared dispatch helpers; do not move a new runtime into core.
5. Host passes trusted policy and opaque connection options. WhatsApp translates policy to sync_history/sync_full_history and concrete storage opts. Preserve false/false and require_ram_schema: true for ZAQ; do not accidentally pass nil/default true from the schematic examples. Persisted ingress cannot override trusted policy. Provider infrastructure starts once, before any provisional/saved connector, using existing provider runtime support. Keep restart policies and readiness behavior unchanged.
6. All sends/edits/typing/reactions/media/DM operations and lifecycle matching use the selected connector's adapter-prepared scope. Never fall back to another profile or require a live listener merely to derive stable identity. Stop/restart retains credentials; authorized explicit logout clears them. Base Bridge delegates provider-specific resolution to the configured bridge instead of naming JidoChatBridge/linked-device details.
7. Replace WhatsApp-specific room admission with a common trusted room reply policy (e.g. mention_required) enabled for WhatsApp while preserving other providers' defaults. Use normalized adapter facts. Do not drop unaddressed messages at the adapter: history capture still needs them. Preserve history suppression before AI/reply hooks, self filtering, DM behavior, message patterns and thread-root rules. Ensure a quoted/group reply cannot evade the current explicit-mention requirement.
8. Keep lifecycle events through existing sink and Jido event routing. Document provider-neutral metadata and validate expected adapter, opaque connector identity, original source PID and attempt. Apply presentation before acknowledging; preserve source-death/stale-event/QR-redaction safeguards.

## End-to-end trace and lifetime invariants
Host authorizes -> Adapter.authenticate -> WhatsApp provisional session/QR -> explicit account confirmation -> shared Authentication.Request(persist) via sink -> existing Engine atomic save -> receipt + opaque binding/runtime -> WhatsApp seeds RAM once -> shared Authentication.Request(start) via same sink -> existing host runtime reconciliation.
Uncertain persist timeout may have committed: retries use the same attempt ID/frozen snapshot. After a committed receipt, seeding/activation failure stays saved with runtime_pending, without repeated persistence or stale snapshot overwrite. Preserve 10-second/remaining-attempt authentication bounds and current storage timeout layering (7-second request, 6-second RPC) unless independently justified/approved.
Synchronous private storage must bypass State: State can be waiting for an outbound adapter call that itself needs storage. Queueing storage as ordinary chat actions can deadlock. A missing explicit runtime must not recursively start listeners. Preserve exact binding checks even for RAM operations and preserve reconnect/storage-generation fencing.

## Action reuse assessment
Authentication commands: REUSE lib/zaq/channels/actions/pair_linked_device.ex / CommunicationBridge.authenticate and Adapter.authenticate. Host reloads super-admin actor for each operation; nil/stale owner or opaque handle alone grants nothing. Adapters own session handles, not ZAQ roles. Code-only confidential boundary; no agent/workflow exposure. Verify negative authorization and non-WhatsApp conformance.
Confirmation: REUSE lib/zaq/engine/actions/confirm_linked_device.ex and Zaq.Engine.LinkedDeviceConfirmation through Event/NodeRouter. Input normalized account, attempt, package-encoded records; output receipt/binding/runtime. Atomic encrypted persistence, operator/provider/account scope and idempotency remain authoritative. Verify uncertain save/repeat confirmation/activation failure.
Credential operations: REUSE lib/zaq/engine/actions/credential_document.ex / Connect.credential_document through confidential runtime Event/NodeRouter dispatch. Binding/provider validation on each request; opaque encrypted values; commit before acknowledgement; preserve missing value versus failure and no blind write retries. No new Action or agent tool. Verify binding substitution, cleared/disabled state and synchronous storage during outbound.
Runtime/normalization: EXTEND existing Adapter behaviour/implementations and CommunicationBridge.sync_config_runtime, JidoChatBridge and State; LOCAL-ONLY transport mapping and supervision wiring, since these are runtime contracts rather than independently exposed business Actions. Existing BridgeSupervisor remains runtime owner. Verify preparation/recovery/outbound isolation and lifecycle ordering.

## Acceptance and rollback
- No Jido.Chat.WhatsApp.* request/module dependency, :whatsapp conditional or WhatsApp transport/storage option interpretation in generic bridge orchestration. Provider registry entries and explicit provider-normalization modules may still name providers; do not expand scope into unrelated normalizers.
- A fake non-WhatsApp adapter demonstrates the identical authentication/storage/infrastructure/lifecycle/connection-options path; Mattermost/Telegram remain compatible without adopting optional features.
- No extra MFA options. No new generic request execution framework, duplicate persistence/Actions, database schema change, new UI, Mnesia policy change or automatic agent-tool exposure.
- Existing relevant observable behavior and tests remain intact. Add focused boundary/property regressions where authorized; no expected-value/fixture/assertion changes without explicit approval. Run default non-live adapter tests, not real WhatsApp traffic.
- Reject/rework if profiles cross, authorization weakens, state reentrancy deadlocks, QR leaks, volatile storage persists to disk, cold restart changes defaults, activation failure loses a receipt or existing tests must be weakened.
- Dependency versions must be reproducible and mutually compatible. No machine-local paths in final manifest. Publication/push needs explicit authorization; local validation is not proof upstream revisions exist.

## Validation and handoff
Each child lists tests to write before implementation, files/branches, edge-only mocking and docs. Follow authoritative docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md validation lifecycle: issue checks, post-review coverage-upper, final precommit before final human approval. Run each package's own quality/default non-live gates in its workspace. No new browser E2E is needed for this refactor; original feature approval/E2E obligations remain with their existing issues. Record exact revisions, test results, coverage gaps and release blockers. No tests were run during this planning task.


## Required policy
Read this epic before starting. Read each affected repository's AGENTS.md. In ZAQ read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/services/channels.md, docs/services/system-config.md and applicable docs/conventions.md; before documentation edits read docs/documentation.md. Run bw prime and verify live source/Git/dependency state. Use Serena for source relationships and Context Mode for large output. Follow docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md#phase-4--validate and its final validation/coverage lifecycle rather than treating this ticket as an alternative policy. No existing test behavior change is approved by this plan. No new feature E2E is planned: this is a behavior-preserving boundary refactor with no UI change. Reassess that decision if scope expands.

## Implementation sequence and dependency graph
1. zaq-973.1: Define shared Jido sink requests and optional adapter contracts
2. zaq-973.2: Migrate WhatsApp internals to the shared sink and adapter contracts
3. zaq-973.3: Replace ZAQ concrete request handling with shared private sink contracts
4. zaq-973.4: Generalize ZAQ runtime, connection options and lifecycle handling
5. zaq-973.5: Replace WhatsApp message branching with a generic room reply policy
6. zaq-973.6: Validate cross-repository compatibility and finalize dependency/documentation handoff

```mermaid
graph LR
  s1["zaq-973.1"]
  s2["zaq-973.2"]
  s3["zaq-973.3"]
  s4["zaq-973.4"]
  s5["zaq-973.5"]
  s6["zaq-973.6"]
  s1 --> s2 --> s3 --> s4 --> s5 --> s6
```
Linear dependencies intentionally serialize the shared contract, producer, host transport, host runtime, policy and integration changes; each depends on the reviewed preceding contract. No diamond/cycle. Only the first child should be initially ready within this epic. Parent aggregation is not an implementation blocker. All tasks remain open; implementation has not started.

comments.text: User said start implementing in this conversation. Implementation is authorized; commit/push/publication remain unauthorized. Local implementation spans ZAQ and sibling jido_chat/jido_chat_whatsapp. Single sink_mfa preserved. Resolved API: adapter prepare_connection/1 retains {:ok, ingress_map}; core wrapper prepare_connection/2 places it into listener keyword opts, preserving legacy opts. Added optional connection_options/2 callback retaining its existing map result; core wrapper normalizes to delivery keyword opts. Dependency manifests restored to checked-in declarations; validation uses targeted local source patches in ignored dependency checkouts. Fresh published core/package pins remain an explicit prerequisite before deployment/merge.
